- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 5–7 days.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast for next 5–7 days.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model overreacts and forecasts higher than true; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak for 3–5 days.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.0% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- Mean reversion is strong in 3–5 day windows; if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses late-period spikes; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for last 5–7 days if sentiment is bullish and price is trending upward.
